properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signature capability ships via tweetnacl@0.14.5, a dependency of sshpk@1.16.1 (yarn.lock line 6672), which web3's HTTP stack pulls through request→http-signature for SSH key parsing/signing. No application call site in src/ (verified: no tweetnacl import in the application). Observable here; replaceable only by bumping the web3/request chain. Shor-vulnerable signature — migrate on the ML-DSA-65 schedule the inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 implements ECDSA on secp256k1 — the signature scheme of the entire Ethereum/web3 stack (transaction and message signing via web3-eth-accounts/ethereumjs-util). The SDK performs no signing itself but ships and exposes the web3 accounts API that does, so downstream applications sign with quantum-unsafe ECDSA. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 also exposes ECDH key agreement (secp256k1), shipped in the bundle via the web3 dependency chain. No direct ECDH call in src/ (grep-verified), but the capability ships. Retroactive (harvest-now-decrypt-later) risk class if used for key establishment. Changeable here via dependency bump; ML-KEM-768 is the migration target for any actual ECDH use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides X25519 scalar-mult (nacl.scalarMult) key agreement. Transitive dep of the web3 stack; no direct import in src/ (grep-verified), but the primitive ships in the bundle. Quantum-unsafe key agreement — retroactive/HNDL risk class if used for key establishment. Changeable here via dependency bump; migration X25519MLKEM768 hybrid.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 password KDF ships via pbkdf2@3.1.2 with three parents in the tree: crypto-browserify@3.12.0 (line 2273), parse-asn1@5.1.6 (line 5655, encrypted-key support), and ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (line 2779, Ethereum keystore/mnemonic derivation). Iteration count and PRF are chosen by the calling libraries at runtime — not pinned anywhere in this repo, which is worth knowing when parameters are audited. Quantum-safe (symmetric KDF); inventory record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 (resolved yarn.lock:6381) implements the scrypt memory-hard password KDF that web3-eth-accounts/ethereumjs-wallet use to derive keys for encrypted Ethereum keystore (v3 wallet JSON) files. Password KDFs are not quantum-broken (Groner gives only square-root on the password search); A- rating appropriate. The parameter set that decides strength (N/r/p) is chosen by the web3 keystore code, not in this repo. Changeable here via dependency bump.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305-256) authenticated encryption — strong classical AE, quantum-relevant only via Grover's square-root on the 256-bit key, hence A+. Transitive dep of the web3 stack; no direct use in src/ (grep-verified), but the primitive ships in the bundle. Changeable here via dependency bump.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TweetNaCl.js at 0.14.5 — unmaintained since 2017 — parent sshpk@1.16.1 (line 6672). Supplies Ed25519, X25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305 and SHA-512 to the HTTP-signature path of web3's `request` dependency. No application import in src/; the shipped dependency tree carries these algorithms whether or not the application calls them. Changeable only via the request→http-signature→sshpk chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS scrypt KDF (3.0.1) is a direct dependency of web3-eth-accounts@1.8.0 (line 7635) and @1.3.6 — the account/signing layer this SDK exposes to consumers through web3. Used for mnemonic/keystore → private-key derivation when consumers create accounts. Changeable here only by upgrading web3.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Streamable SHA-1/SHA-2 hashes (2.4.11); parents create-hash@1.2.0 (line 2223) and create-hmac@1.1.7 (line 2234) inside the crypto-browserify polyfill that web3-eth-accounts ships into the browser bundle. No application call site in src/; presence is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Package-level entry for the elliptic library — the EC provider (secp256k1) for the whole web3/ethereumjs stack this SDK depends on. Kept distinct from the algorithm-level entries ALG-710f61f0 (ECDSA) and ALG-c9ffc8a8 (ECDH), which describe the two primitives this same lockfile entry ships; this entry is what a reader bumps when upgrading the provider. Version 6.5.4 is the latest 6.x line. Changeable here via yarn resolutions.
